LM1117 p14 reopened visually: section 9 Application and Implementation opens with the boxed Note read verbatim - Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness. TI customers are responsible for determining suitability of components for their purposes, as well as validating and testing their design implementation to confirm system functionality. The record quotes the load-bearing fragment exactly. The scope claim is right too: 9.5.1.1 Heat Sink Requirements is a subsection of section 9 (starts p17, runs onto p18), so the eq 2-5 sizing chain this record prescribes does inherit the disclaimer, and the citation note states it in those terms. I also reopened LM1117 p18 this pass for the sibling thermal record and it still carries what this record cites: eq 2 IIN = IL + IG, eq 3 PD = (VIN-VOUT)IL + VIN IG with Fig 9-10 Power Dissipation Diagram, eq 4 TR(max) = TJ(max)-TA(max), eq 5 RthJA = TR(max)/PD, and As a design aid, Table 9-2 shows the value of the theta_JA of SOT-223 and TO-252 for different heat sink area, with the page naming AN1028 for power enhancement techniques - which is also why the AN-1028 material this record carries is fairly attached. linear-regulator-esr-zero-compensation.note: Post-verification edit re-read, and all five cited pages re-read this pass. The added SLVA115A p3 holds exactly: p3 carries the window as numbers (The curve of this device requires that, for the minimum 2.2-uF of output capacitance, the ESR must be between 0.1 ohm and 20 ohm), the worked fZ(ESR) = 1/(2 pi RESR COUT) = 72.3 kHz with RESR 0.1 ohm and COUT 2.2 uF, the stable ESR-times-C product band, the sentence Few capacitors have more than 2 ohm of ESR so the upper limit on the ESR can usually be ignored, AND the load-transient method - Performing a load transient test and observing the amount of ringing on the output is the best way to determine if the capacitor selected is stable - with Figure 3 Load Transient Setup drawn as a MOSFET switch plus function generator and the sentence This setup is preferable to most electronic loads because the simulated transient is much faster. That closes the prior citation slip. The reduced p4 note also holds: p4 carries only Figure 4 TPS76050 Load Transient With 2.2-uF Ceramic Capacitor and the text The results in Figure 4 show multiple oscillations or rings after the initial spike, indicating instability ... Typically, four rings or less indicate sufficient phase margin for the device to be stable; the jig is no longer claimed for p4. Re-checked the rest: p1 names the three poles (dominant pole set in the error amplifier, load pole P(LOAD) formed by the output capacitor and load and therefore varies with load current, pass device pole P(PASS) formed by the parasitic capacitance of the pass element), states that a three-pole high gain system requires compensation, and calls using the ESR of the output capacitor typically the simplest and least expensive method for generating this zero, with the abstract scoping the whole report to LDO regulators with PNP or PMOS pass element; p2 Fig 1 carries the labelled Dominant Pole P(DOM), P(LOAD) with its Variation in R(LOAD) x C(LOAD) arrow, fZ(ESR) with its Variation in C(LOAD) x ESR arrow and P(PASS) near 1 MHz, the paragraph beneath gives both bounds (high enough that the 0 dB crossing is -20 dB/decade, low enough that gain is below 0 dB before P(PASS)), Fig 2 is the TPS76050 region of stability at CO = 2.2 uF and TJ = 25 C, and the NOTE reads The ESR used in these plots is the minimum ESR of the capacitor as ESR does vary over frequency; p5 Fig 5 is the same 2.2-uF ceramic plus a 1-ohm series resistor, settling without the ring train. Principle level with rule null and no envelope is right, and the PNP/PMOS provenance is disclosed in prose. Free strengthener for a later pass: the p6 Conclusion states the same convention more broadly - When designing with older linear regulators ... As the ESR is a function of frequency, the minimum ESR is used in simulations - without the these plots qualifier.

linear-regulator-fixed-variant-min-load.note: Re-read AMS p1/p2/p3/p4/p5/p6 and LM1117 p5/p6, pressing on the Device cell. AMS p3: the Minimum Load Current row Device cell reads "AMS1117" alone (5 typ / 10 max mA, Note 5) while Current Limit, Quiescent Current and Dropout list -1.5/-1.8/-2.5/-2.85/-3.3/-5.0 - as the note says. Two independent checks remove the ambiguity. (1) AMS p1 ORDERING INFORMATION lists bare AMS1117 as its own SOT-223 orderable part, the adjustable, so that Device cell names a device and not the family; the other bare-AMS1117 rows are ADJ-only parameters (Reference Voltage at IOUT=10 mA, Adjust Pin Current, the CADJ=10 uF ripple row). (2) AMS p2 conditions the adjustable Load Regulation row on 10mA <= IOUT <= 0.8A while every fixed row reads 0 <= IOUT <= 0.8A, and the fixed Output Voltage rows (AMS1117-3.3: 3.201/3.300/3.399 V at VIN=4.8V) inherit the table header "at IOUT = 0 mA" - the fixed part is guaranteed at zero load, which Note 5 cannot simultaneously forbid. TI is explicit rather than inferential: LM1117 p6 scopes the Minimum load current row to "LM1117-ADJ" (1.7 typ at 25 C, 5 max over temp) and gives -1.8/-2.5/-3.3/-5.0 quiescent-current rows instead; p5 specifies LM1117-3.3 over 0 <= IOUT <= 800 mA with line regulation at IOUT = 0 mA, while every ADJ row starts at 10 mA. AMS p6 curve title is verbatim "Minimum Operating Current (Adjustable Device)", flat at about 6 mA (TJ 25 C) and 8 mA (125 C) across 0-20 V differential, with no fixed-device equivalent on the page. AMS p4 verbatim: the R1/R2 current "is normally the specified minimum load current of 10mA"; AMS p5 verbatim: "In the case of fixed voltage devices the top of R1 is connected Kelvin internally". Dropout numbers match the pages (AMS 1.1 typ / 1.3 max at 0.8 A with Note 4 stopping at 0.8 A; LM1117 p6 1.15 typ at 500 mA, 1.25 over temp, 1.2 at 800 mA), and the headroom arithmetic (4.75 - 3.3 = 1.45 V vs 1.3 V max) is right. Envelope iout_a max 0.8 is exactly where both datasheets stop specifying. The not-required bleed is scoped to fixed 1117-class parts in applies, not claimed in general.

linear-regulator-live-tab-thermal-vias.note: Post-verification edit re-read, and all five cited pages re-read this pass. The required disclosure is present in envelope_note and is honest - Disclosure: no VIN-tab part appears in this task ledger, so vin is included on MECHANISM alone (a via between two different nets is a short whichever nets they are) and not on the strength of any page read - naming both the absence and the basis, and leaving rule tab_net vout resting on its pages. Re-checked every citation. AMS p1 PIN CONNECTIONS gives 1 Ground/Adjust, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN, the TO-252 FRONT VIEW is annotated TAB IS OUTPUT, and the 8L SOIC top view carries four VOUT pins. LM1117 p3 Figure 6-1 (DCY package, 4-Pin SOT, top view) is drawn with the tab labelled Tab is VOUT, and Table 6-1 gives VOUT as SOT-223 pins 2, 4 with TO-252, TO-263 and TO-220 all reading 2, TAB, and pin 1 ADJ/GND described as Adjust pin for adjustable output option. Ground pin for fixed output option. Precision worth carrying: for SOT-223 the table says 2, 4 without the word TAB, so pin 4 = tab is established by Figure 6-1 rather than by the table. AN-1028 p4 reads verbatim For maximum performance, it is recommended to put extra copper on the bottom of the board connected to the top pad by through-hole thermal vias, with the conclusion bullet that placement of the copper pads on the top side of the board gives the best thermal performance. AN-1028 p8 reads verbatim For layouts with copper on the top and bottom planes, there are 0.02 inch copper plated vias (heat pipes) connecting the two planes, so the two-sided vendor data does presume a galvanic stitch. AMS p5 reads verbatim Experiments have shown that the heat spreading copper layer does not need to be electrically connected to the tab of the device. The PC material can be very effective at transmitting heat between the pad area, attached to the pad of the device, and a ground plane layer either inside or on the opposite side of the board. Both consequences in prose follow from those pages rather than from generic advice. Topology level with the envelope on tab_net_kind alone is right.

linear-regulator-tab-copper-area-theta-j.note: Delta pass on the post-verification edit (mtime 19:36 vs verdict 19:28): section-9 clause, LM1117 p14 citation, the new 45 C/W clause, and the trim. All four hold. LM1117 p14 reopened: the boxed Note opening section 9 reads verbatim Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness; Table 9-2, Fig 9-11 and Fig 9-13 all sit in 9.5.1.1 inside that section, so the citation scope claim is exact. AMS p5 reopened for the 45 C/W clause: The thermal resistance from the junction to the tab for the AMS1117 is 15 C/W. The thermal resistance from tab to ambient can be as low as 30 C/W - and the page states the sum ITSELF, The total thermal resistance from junction to ambient can be as low as 45 C/W. This requires a reasonable sized PC board with at least on layer of copper to spread the heat across the board and couple it into the surrounding air. So 45 total on a well-coppered board is the page own sentence rather than record arithmetic, and 55 C/W is demonstrably not a package floor. The trim claim checks out number by number. Everything still in prose sits on its page: AMS p5 Table 1 rows 1000/0/1000 = 65, 1000/1000/1000 = 60, 1000/2500/2500 = 55, 100/2500/2500 = 80, footnote Tab of device attached to topside copper, 1/16 in FR-4 with 1 oz copper foil as a rough guideline; AMS p2 SOT-223 theta_JA 90 C/W with the footnote that with package soldering to copper area over backside ground plane or internal power plane it can vary from 46 C/W to >90 C/W; LM1117 p18 Table 9-2 0.0123 = 136, 0.3 = 84, 1 sq in = 66 (1 sq in = 645 sq mm, so the agreement with AMS 1000 sq mm = 65 is fair); p19 splits 0.066+0.066 = 125 through 0.5+0.5 = 70, totals 0.132/0.35/0.568/0.784/1.0, Fig 9-11 ranking Top Cu lowest across the sweep, Fig 9-13 six curves 136, 123, 84, 75, 69, 66 with the 66 curve at about 1.5 W at TA 25 C. The dropped numbers are all still in citation notes and none was load-bearing. AMS 225/2500/2500 = 65 remains in the p5 note; no rule key used it, and the two ladders that carry claims are intact - the back-side ladder 65 -> 60 -> 55 (the about 5 C/W claim) and the top-area ladder 100 = 80 vs 1000 = 55. TI 0.066 = 123, 0.53 = 75, 0.76 = 69 remain in the p18 note and again in the p19 Fig 9-13 curve list, while the endpoints 136 and 66 plus the mid point 84 stay in prose, which is all the cross-check with AMS needs. All five rule keys still land on their rows: 90, 65, 60, 55, 66. Two standing caveats unchanged and still flagged by the record: LM1117 Fig 9-11 and 9-13 are captioned 1 oz while the AN-1028 boards behind the same 16 layouts were 2 oz clad, and the 1.5 W envelope max marks where retrieval stops, never a permitted dissipation ((125-50)/55 = 1.36 W at TA 50 C).

linear-regulator-1117-output-cap-esr-win.note: Third pass. Every cited page reopened visually and the WHOLE prose re-read hunting for the relocated dielectric claim: none survives. The CONSEQUENCE paragraph is now a pure restatement of LM1117 p15 - a candidate qualifies only if ITS OWN datasheet puts ESR inside 0.3-22 ohm, under 0.3 ohm is outside - followed by the admission that no source here states a dielectric family ESR and that the concrete part is a P3 question. The only dielectric names left in prose are vendor words: tantalum from LM1117 p15 (The minimum output capacitance required by the LM1117 is 10 uF, if a tantalum capacitor is used) and AMS p4 (The addition of 22uF solid tantalum on the output will ensure stability for all operating conditions), and ceramic only inside the verbatim SLVA115A p6 quote about NEWER LDOs. Nothing asserts or implies what any capacitor technology ESR IS. Negative claim checked exhaustively by text search of all four PDFs: polymer, MLCC, multilayer, X7R and X5R occur in none of them; ceramic occurs only in SLVA115A; the string ESR occurs in LM1117 on p15 alone and NOWHERE in the AMS datasheet - so neither 1117 datasheet carries an ESR-vs-IOUT chart or a measurement frequency, as the record says. Rule keys re-verified on their pages: p15 sec 9.2.2.1.3 verbatim - must meet the required conditions for both minimum amount of capacitance and equivalent series resistance (ESR), the 10 uF tantalum minimum, The ESR of the output capacitor should range between 0.3 ohm to 22 ohm, and In the case of the adjustable regulator, when the CADJ is used, a larger output capacitance (22-uF tantalum) is required; LM1117 p14 sec 9.2.2.1.1 gives A 10-uF tantalum on the input is a suitable input capacitor for almost all applications; AMS p4 gives 22 uF solid tantalum with no ESR bound on the page; AMS p3 conditions every ripple-rejection row (AMS1117-3.3: 60 min / 72 typ at VIN 4.75 V) on COUT = 22 uF Tantalum, IOUT = 1 A. Both new citations hold. LM1117 p14 carries the boxed section-9 Note verbatim - Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness - and 9.2.2.1.3 sits inside section 9, so PROVENANCE is right. SLVA115A p6 Conclusion reads verbatim - When designing with older linear regulators, ESR is very important to consider when selecting the output capacitor. As the ESR is a function of frequency, the minimum ESR is used in simulations. Newer LDOs like the TPS7A26 device are inherently ceramic capacitor stable - and it IS broader than the p2 NOTE, which qualifies the same convention with in these plots. The AMS p4 extensions are verbatim: The value of 22uF tantalum covers all cases of bypassing the adjustment terminal, and Without bypassing the adjustment terminal smaller capacitors can be used with equally good results - exactly what the prose concludes (22 uF conservative rather than mandatory for a part with no adjust terminal to bypass; TI tantalum floor 10 uF). Three precisions for later, none load-bearing. (1) CONSEQUENCE says at the operating point while INFERENCE prescribes the minimum ESR over frequency - two different tests, and no page states either condition; keep the INFERENCE wording if one must win. (2) SLVA115A p4, NOT cited here, calls the DUT a 2.2-uF ceramic (low ESR) capacitor - the nearest page evidence that a dielectric is low ESR, still qualitative and about one part, so the record negative claim stands, but a future pass wanting to name typical failures now has p4 plus p3 rather than nothing. (3) envelope_note keeps one dielectric sentence - for a ceramic-stable LDO a bare MLCC is the correct part - but it is out-of-envelope scoping and its content is on SLVA115A p6 (inherently ceramic capacitor stable, improving cost, size and performance) and p3 (no need to be concerned about ESR); only the acronym MLCC is the record own wording. Same for a FIXED 1117 has no adjust terminal: true in the ledger (LM1117 p3 Table 6-1, AMS p5) but on pages this record does not cite.
